blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Indian Railways was nationalised in 1951 and is currently divided into 19 administrative zones.
The first passenger train ran between Bori Bunder (Bombay) and Thane on April 16, 1853.
Lord Dalhousie is considered the Father of Indian Railways.
Bholu, the guard elephant, serves as the official mascot of Indian Railways.
The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway was the first mountain railway in India to receive UNESCO World Heritage status in 1999.
